programmes.name: Diploma in Business Practice (Customer Experience & Relationship Management)
programmes.skills: Service management, service marketing, CX design & management, customer intelligence, data analytics, issues management
programmes.rationale: This is NYP's own reference programme — not benchmarked against itself.

programmes.name: Customer Experience Innovation (SCTP module)
programmes.skills: Customer journey mapping, gap analysis, CX improvement implementation
programmes.rationale: This is a standalone NYP module offering, drawn directly from the Customer Experience Design module in MC5 — it is NYP's own content, not a competitor comparison.

programmes.name: Service Management (SCTP module)
programmes.skills: Complaint management, service guarantees, service quality assurance
programmes.rationale: This is a standalone NYP module offering, drawn directly from the Service Operations and Issues Management modules in MC3 — NYP's own content, not a competitor comparison.

programmes.name: Specialist Diploma in Customer Experience Design and Analytics
programmes.skills: Customer & guest management, UX, branding, service marketing, relationship management, CX analytics
programmes.rationale: Matched: customer & guest management and CX analytics map onto Customer Experience Design and Customer Intelligence & Analytics; relationship management maps onto Customer Management & Retention; branding/UX psychology maps onto Consumer Psychology. Capped by: no coverage of NYP's business-essentials modules (statistics, accounting, applied economics) or people/team management — it's a pure CX/marketing specialist diploma, not a broader business diploma.

programmes.name: Customer Service Management (modular unit, Dip. Business Practice - Business Admin)
programmes.skills: Frontline & contact centre service excellence, complaint handling, service philosophy
programmes.cert: Statement of Result → Diploma in Business Practice
programmes.rationale: Matched: frontline and contact-centre service excellence maps onto Service Operations; complaint handling and service guarantees map onto Issues Management. Capped by: no CX design, digital marketing, or analytics content — this is a single entry-level modular unit, not a full diploma.

programmes.name: Specialist Diploma in Digital Marketing & Analytics (NSDMA)
programmes.skills: Digital marketing strategy & analytics, social media marketing, e-commerce, brand visibility
programmes.rationale: Matched: digital marketing strategy and analytics maps onto Digital Marketing and Market Research & Intelligence. Capped by: no service management, CX design, or stakeholder relationship content — this is a marketing specialist diploma, not a service/CX one.

programmes.name: SP-SUSS Specialist Diploma in Digital Content Marketing (incl. Work-Study pathway)
programmes.fee: Course fee + AP funding for employers
programmes.skills: Content creation, social media management, branding, marketing communications
programmes.rationale: Matched: content creation and social media management map onto the content-marketing angle of Digital Marketing. Capped by: no service, CX design, or customer analytics content at all — narrowly focused on content production.

programmes.name: Customer Relationship Management (BUS354)
programmes.skills: Customer lifecycle strategy, CRM data & segmentation, IDIC framework, customer analytics
programmes.rationale: Matched: customer lifecycle strategy and CRM data/segmentation map onto Customer Intelligence & Analytics and Customer Management & Retention; the IDIC framework (Identify, Differentiate, Interact, Customise) maps onto Stakeholder Relationship Management. Capped by: no CX experience-design (journey mapping, service blueprinting) or service-marketing execution content — strong on relationship/data strategy, narrower on design and marketing execution.

programmes.name: Customer Experience Management (Graduate Diploma module)
programmes.skills: CX assessment, organisation-wide CX process design
programmes.cert: Stackable to Graduate Diploma in Management
programmes.rationale: Matched: CX assessment and organisation-wide CX process design map closely onto Customer Experience Design — a near 1:1 conceptual match. Capped by: it's a single graduate-level module, so it doesn't extend into customer intelligence/analytics, retention, or the service/marketing MCs — high match quality, narrow scope.

programmes.name: Integrated Marketing Communications (MKT358)
programmes.skills: IMC strategy, PR, corporate communication, creative advertising & copywriting
programmes.rationale: Matched: campaign and communications execution partially maps onto Digital Marketing; professional messaging skills touch Business Communication. Capped by: the course's core focus — PR, advertising, copywriting — sits outside NYP's CXRM scope entirely, which doesn't teach traditional advertising/PR craft.

programmes.name: Master of Digital Marketing / Graduate Certificate in Digital Marketing
programmes.skills: SEO/SEM, social, e-commerce, marketing analytics, strategy/analytics/design clusters
programmes.rationale: Matched: SEO/SEM and marketing analytics map onto Digital Marketing and Market Research & Intelligence. Capped by: postgraduate depth (advanced analytics, strategy/design specialisation clusters) goes well beyond NYP's single-module treatment of digital marketing — relative overlap is modest despite topical alignment.

programmes.name: Specialist Certificate in Digital Content Marketing
programmes.level: Specialist Certificate → stackable to BSc Marketing
programmes.duration: Modular, up to 3 yrs to complete
programmes.skills: Content marketing, digital storytelling
programmes.cert: Specialist Certificate, pathway to BSc Marketing
programmes.rationale: Matched: content marketing and storytelling map onto a narrow slice of Digital Marketing. Capped by: no service, CX, or analytics content — a single-topic specialist certificate.

programmes.name: Work-Study Post-Diploma (WSPostDip) programmes
programmes.skills: Varies by track; credits stack toward SUSS degree
programmes.rationale: Matched: varies by track, but where CX/service tracks apply, maps onto Service Operations and Customer Experience Design. Capped by: track-dependent — some WSPostDip tracks run in unrelated disciplines entirely, so this is a directional average across the CX/RM/Marketing-relevant tracks only.

programmes.name: Customer Experience Management (Level 1 & 2, WSQ)
programmes.skills: L1: CX & CRM fundamentals; L2: CRM data use, loyalty, inventory, sales targets
programmes.rationale: Matched: CRM data use and loyalty programme content map onto Customer Management & Retention; CX/CRM fundamentals map onto Stakeholder Relationship Management (foundational level). Capped by: retail-floor content — inventory management, sales targets, running a store — sits outside NYP's diploma scope, which doesn't cover retail operations.

programmes.name: SkillsFuture Series Certificate of Competency (Business & Service track)
programmes.skills: Design thinking for service, business fundamentals, wellness/hospitality service skills
programmes.rationale: Matched: design thinking for service touches Customer Experience Design conceptually. Capped by: this is a short, generic Certificate of Competency, not a deep service/CX curriculum — minimal structured overlap.

programmes.name: Work-Study Diploma in Customer Experience Management (Lifestyle & Consumer)
programmes.funding: WSDip: employer-funded via SWDA, ETSS up to 90% for SMEs, ITE Opportunity Fund
programmes.skills: Consumer behaviour analysis, personalised customer content, sales & e-commerce services, service experience & UX design, customer service & quality, digital marketing operations, AI solutions
programmes.rationale: Matched: consumer behaviour analysis and personalised content map onto Customer Experience Design and Customer Intelligence & Analytics; digital marketing operations maps onto Digital Marketing; customer/stakeholder communication maps onto Stakeholder Relationship Management — the broadest match of any ITE Work-Study Diploma, spanning 3 MCs. Capped by: the AI-solutions-development outcome has no equivalent NYP module (NYP's diploma has no dedicated AI content), and this ITE diploma stops short of NYP's deeper analytics/retention modules.

programmes.name: Work-Study Diploma in Customer Experience Management (Aviation Services)
programmes.funding: WSDip: employer-funded via SWDA, ETSS up to 90% for SMEs
programmes.skills: Complex service request handling, design thinking, customer/service data analytics, team leadership, continuous improvement in high-volume service operations
programmes.rationale: Matched: complex service request handling maps onto Service Operations; design-thinking elements partially map onto Customer Experience Design. Capped by: sector-specific aviation operations knowledge and team leadership in high-volume operations sit outside NYP's generalist CXRM diploma scope.

programmes.name: Work-Study Diploma in E-commerce & Retail
programmes.funding: WSDip: employer-funded via SWDA, ETSS up to 90% for SMEs
programmes.skills: In-store retail ops, customer immersive experience & service innovation, category management, e-commerce ops & marketing, retail analytics, business strategy, leadership
nypModules: Data Analytics for Strategic Business Decisions
programmes.rationale: Matched: e-commerce operations & marketing maps onto Digital Marketing; customer immersive experience & service innovation maps onto Service Operations; category management/business strategy maps onto Marketing Management; retail analytics maps onto Data Analytics for Strategic Business Decisions. Capped by: in-store retail operations, logistics & supply chain, and leadership/people management (3 of 8 listed learning outcomes) have no equivalent in NYP's CXRM diploma, which is service/CX/marketing-focused rather than a retail-operations or supply-chain qualification.

programmes.name: Work-Study Diploma in Media Communication & Digital Marketing
programmes.funding: WSDip: employer-funded via SWDA, ETSS up to 90% for SMEs
programmes.skills: Digital content development for service marketing, brand & content marketing, social media campaigns, email marketing, video advertisement production
programmes.rationale: Matched: digital content development for service marketing maps onto Digital Marketing. Capped by: graphic design, video production, and animation skills — core to this ITE diploma — sit entirely outside NYP's diploma, which doesn't teach content-production tools.

programmes.name: SIM Academy executive & business programmes (CX / people mgmt strand)
programmes.skills: Applied CX & leadership, digital transformation crossover, people management
programmes.rationale: Matched: leadership/people management crossover maps onto People and Team Management; applied CX content partially maps onto Service Operations. Capped by: SIM's digital-transformation content and broad executive-education catalogue (600+ courses) sit largely outside the CXRM diploma's specific scope — this is an executive-education generalist, not a CX specialist.

programmes.name: ClickAcademy Asia — Customer Engagement & Digital Marketing tracks
programmes.skills: B2B sales, digital marketing, customer engagement, AI-in-marketing
programmes.rationale: Matched: digital marketing and AI-in-marketing content partially maps onto Digital Marketing. Capped by: B2B sales content and generic 'customer engagement' framing don't map onto any specific NYP module — largely a corporate-training generalist rather than CX-curriculum-aligned.

programmes.name: Singapore Airlines Academy — bespoke CX capability programmes (e.g. AIA Singapore partnership)
programmes.skills: CX culture transformation, service mindset, storytelling, scenario-based service excellence
programmes.rationale: Matched: CX culture transformation and service mindset are thematically adjacent to Service Excellence Project and Customer Experience Design. Capped by: this is bespoke, non-formal corporate delivery with no public syllabus — the match is conceptual/thematic only, not curricular, hence the lowest score in the tracker.

nypModuleRegistry.module: Data Analytics for Strategic Business Decisions
Optimising Business Operations with Essential Technology

Work-Study Diploma in E-commerce & Retai: Data Analytics for Strategic Business Decisions

competitors.name: Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS)
competitors.role: Highest direct overlap — university-level CX, RM and Marketing CET spanning courses to Master's
points: Deep, stackable ladder: Specialist Certificate → Grad Cert → Grad Dip → Master's in Digital Marketing
BUS354 Customer Relationship Management and MGT554 Customer Experience Management run as credit-bearing, stackable CET courses
Only university with formal Work-Study Post-Diploma agreements with all 5 polytechnics
Positioning: degree-pathway CET — appeals to learners wanting academic progression, not just a certificate

competitors.name: Republic Polytechnic
points: Specialist Diploma in Customer Experience Design and Analytics, co-developed with SUSS
Explicitly covers relationship management, service marketing and business development — near-identical territory to NYP's Diploma in Business Practice (CX&RM)
SUSS co-development gives it a credible analytics/academic hook

competitors.name: Singapore Polytechnic
competitors.role: Strong in digital marketing, less in core CX/service
points: Specialist Diploma in Digital Marketing & Analytics (NSDMA) leverages both Business and Media/Design schools
SP-SUSS Work-Study pathway into Digital Content Marketing gives it a fresh-grad talent pipeline story
Also expanding into Industrial AI training (Oct 2026) — signals appetite for AI-adjacent CET expansion generally

competitors.name: Temasek Polytechnic
competitors.role: Entry/modular service excellence, stackable to full diploma
points: Customer Service Management modular unit stacks into Diploma in Business Practice (Business Administration)
Positioned as an accessible, lower-cost entry point rather than a specialist CX qualification
Runs its CET arm as the Temasek SkillsFuture Academy (TSA)

competitors.name: ITE (short courses)
points: Customer Experience Management Level 1 & 2 (WSQ) targets retail frontline and entry-level roles
Positioned as a feeder pathway — skills build toward store/floor management competencies
Broad SkillsFuture Series CoC catalogue includes service-adjacent design thinking modules

competitors.name: ITE (Work-Study Diplomas)
competitors.role: Fully employer-funded fresh-graduate pipeline — a structurally different competitive model, not a fee-based course
points: 4 relevant WSDip tracks found: CX Management (Lifestyle & Consumer), CX Management (Aviation Services), E-commerce & Retail, and Media Communication & Digital Marketing — all 30 months, day-release + on-the-job training

Programme fees are fully employer-sponsored (not learner-paid); SMEs get up to 90% funding via ETSS, on top of per-trainee support up to $15,000 for earlier intakes — a fundamentally different funding model to diploma/specialist-diploma CET

Curriculum reaches notably further into commercial/analytics territory than typical WSQ short courses — e.g. E-commerce & Retail WSDip covers retail analytics, category management and business strategy, not just frontline service
Named retail partners already in place (DFI Retail Group, Uniqlo, Sephora, Skechers) — signals live employer demand NYP could tap for its own work-study conversations
Competes for the same fresh-ITE-graduate talent pool NYP's own Work-Study Certificate programmes target — worth comparing pipeline overlap directly

competitors.name: SIM Academy
points: 600+ course catalogue, 10,000+ professionals trained annually — high volume, high brand recognition
Positions CX within broader leadership/digital transformation/people management programming rather than as a standalone specialism
Active industry-partnership model aligned to national workforce priorities

competitors.name: Industry academies (e.g. Singapore Airlines Academy)
competitors.role: Bespoke, high-prestige B2B CX capability building — not in the public course directory
points: SIA Academy's AIA Singapore engagement shows industry academies competing for large-enterprise CX transformation contracts, not individual learners
These programmes sit outside MySkillsFuture / SkillsFuture funding — a different competitive lane (bespoke consulting-style delivery, brand-led)
Represents both a competitive threat for large-enterprise partnerships and a potential co-delivery partner model to study

trends.h: AI-in-CX is the fastest-rising skill demand signal
trends.p: SSG's 2025/2026 skills-cluster analysis shows Generative AI Principles and Applications as the fastest-growing skill nationally, and financial services / service sectors are actively deploying AI for chatbots, personalisation and robo-advisory within CX functions.

trends.h: Service excellence demand is broadening beyond retail/hospitality
trends.p: SSG's Skills Insights 2026 notes customer service excellence demand thriving across fulfilment operations, engineering services and healthcare/social services client-centric care — not just traditional frontline retail roles.

trends.h: SSG has tightened course funding guidelines from 31 Dec 2025
trends.p: Funding for courses developing 'currently-demanded skills for a current job' is now more tightly scrutinised; SkillsFuture Series (emerging skills) and SCTP/qualification-level courses are exempt from the tightening — favouring programmes framed around emerging or career-transition skillsets.

Creates a single statutory board for training subsidies and career/employment services — likely to affect how CET providers coordinate funding applications with placement and hiring-incentive schemes going forward.

trends.h: Employer sentiment: skills scarcity in sales & marketing roles
trends.p: ManpowerGroup's 2025 Talent Shortage Survey cites Sales & Marketing among the roles most affected by skilled-talent shortages in Singapore (83% of employers report difficulty finding skilled talent, up from 79%).
trends.s: ManpowerGroup 2025 Talent Shortage Survey (via SIM Academy)

trends.h: Micro-credentials gaining ground over full qualifications for hiring
trends.p: Reported that a majority of Singapore employers now weight micro-certifications and demonstrable skills more heavily than traditional academic credentials in fast-moving skill areas — a pressure point for full-diploma-format CET design.
trends.s: Ministry of Manpower data (cited in employer skills coverage)

funding.p: Catalogue expanding to ~200 WSQ full-qualification courses for mid-career Singaporeans aged 40+, spanning Healthcare, ICT, Engineering, Media and Early Childhood — worth watching whether Business/Service Excellence categories are added.

New portal includes AI-powered chatbot guidance, curated in-demand-skill recommendations and occupation-based course exploration — changes how learners discover CET programmes, with implications for course titling/SEO and how differentiated a programme needs to look.

funding.h: Six months of free premium AI tool access for selected courses
funding.p: Learners completing selected AI-linked courses get complimentary premium AI tool subscriptions — a strong incentive lever if NYP builds an AI-augmented CX/service module.

funding.h: Enterprise Innovation Scheme: 400% tax deduction on AI expenditure
funding.p: Capped at $50,000 per YA for FY2027-28 — relevant when pitching employer-sponsored, AI-enabled CX/service transformation training to corporate partners.

funding.h: Adult Educator Registry CPD requirement from 1 April 2026
funding.p: Trainers on SSG-supported courses must complete 40 hrs CPD / 80 hrs practice every two years to remain registered — a quality bar that raises the operating cost of running SSG-funded CET, and a differentiator NYP can lean on if its own trainer bench is strong.

gaps.p: No provider scanned has a dedicated, publicly-listed AI-in-CX module (chatbot design, AI-assisted service recovery, AI personalisation ethics) despite this being SSG's fastest-growing skill cluster and a live funding priority. NYP's existing CX&RM diploma could be refreshed with an AI-in-CX modular certificate, positioned to qualify for SkillsFuture Series (emerging skill) funding rather than the tightened 'current job skill' category.

SSG data shows service excellence demand broadening into fulfilment, engineering services and healthcare client-centric care — sectors where ITE, SP and TP's current service modules are largely retail-framed. A sector-agnostic or B2B/industrial service excellence track is comparatively unclaimed territory.

gaps.t: Mid-career, short-form CX leadership (not full diploma)
gaps.p: SIM Academy's model (600+ short courses, high annual throughput) shows strong demand for bite-sized executive CX/leadership content. NYP's current CX&RM offering is diploma-heavy (900 hrs); a stackable short-course leadership track could capture the SIM-style executive learner NYP is currently not well positioned to serve.

Industry academies (e.g. Singapore Airlines Academy x AIA) are winning large-enterprise CX capability contracts outside the public funding system entirely. This is a different competitive lane — worth exploring as a co-delivery or advisory partnership model rather than a head-to-head course offering.

SUSS's BUS354 and its Master of Digital Marketing analytics cluster suggest a university-level pull toward customer analytics; NYP's CX&RM diploma covers data analytics as one MC among five. A deeper, stackable customer-intelligence/analytics specialisation could defend NYP's ground against SUSS's degree-pathway pull.

partners.name: AIA Singapore × Singapore Airlines Academy model
partners.role: Reference case for a bespoke, large-enterprise CX capability partnership
points: Shows an insurer partnering with a service-brand academy rather than an IHL — a competitive signal and a template NYP could pitch to similarly-sized enterprise clients
Workshops structured around mindset transformation + practical technique — a format NYP's Centre for Industry & Lifelong Learning (CIL3) could replicate for named accounts

partners.name: Alibaba Cloud (existing NYP relationship)
partners.role: Extend from cloud/AI education into AI-powered CX applications
points: NYP already partners with Alibaba Cloud on cloud computing/AI education for students — a natural extension into AI-in-CX applied modules (chatbots, personalisation) for the CET portfolio

partners.name: Mediacorp / SGAG / Mothership (existing NYP relationships via Media & Communication Management)
partners.role: Marketing/content-side partnerships to extend into CX-adjacent content strategy CET
points: Existing internship/project relationships from the Diploma in Media & Communication Management could be extended into CET-level content marketing or brand-experience short courses

partners.name: SSG / WSSG (post-merger)
partners.role: Policy and funding-alignment partner as the WSSG merger completes in Q4 2026
points: Early engagement on how Business/Service Excellence categories fit the expanded SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme catalogue could position NYP courses for inclusion ahead of competitors

summaryThreats.t: Republic Polytechnic's Specialist Diploma in CX Design & Analytics (78% overlap)
summaryThreats.p: Near-identical territory to NYP's flagship CX&RM diploma, co-developed with SUSS for added academic credibility — the single highest-overlap competitor programme tracked.

summaryThreats.t: SUSS's BUS354 Customer Relationship Management (72% overlap)
summaryThreats.p: Credit-bearing and stackable to a full degree — appeals to learners wanting academic progression that NYP's diploma-only structure doesn't offer.

summaryThreats.t: SIM Academy's high-volume executive short-course model
summaryThreats.p: 600+ courses, 10,000+ learners/year in bite-sized formats NYP's diploma-heavy portfolio doesn't currently match (individual overlap is low, but aggregate reach is high).

summaryOpps.p: Fastest-growing SSG skill cluster, no direct competitor coverage found, and aligned to current funding priorities (SkillsFuture Series, AI tool subsidies).
Demand broadening into fulfilment, engineering services and healthcare — largely unclaimed by retail-framed competitor offerings.
Could capture the SIM-style executive learner segment NYP's current diploma format is not built to serve.

specs.t: Enrolment & completion volumes per competitor programme
specs.p: MySkillsFuture shows 'have attended' counts for some courses but not full enrolment trends over time — would need SSG TPGateway data access or IHL peer-benchmarking exchanges to track properly.

specs.t: NYP's own enrolment, revenue and completion data by programme
specs.p: Pull from NYP's internal CET/CIL3 systems to sit alongside this external landscape view, so gap analysis compares actual NYP performance against market activity, not just curriculum content.

specs.t: Job posting / hiring demand data for CX, RM, marketing and service roles
specs.p: MyCareersFuture or LinkedIn Talent Insights data on job posting volumes, salary bands and skill tags for target job families — sharper signal than course-supply data alone for spotting real gaps.
A quarterly snapshot of competitor fee changes (post-subsidy) to catch pricing repositioning early — currently a one-time snapshot in this dashboard.
Malaysia (HRD Corp-funded), Indonesia (Kartu Prakerja) and Hong Kong (CEF) equivalents for CX/service/marketing training, useful if NYP considers regional CET delivery or transnational partnerships.

specs.t: Alumni / employer satisfaction and outcomes data
specs.p: Graduate employment rate and starting salary data (from Graduate Employment Survey equivalents for CET, where available) to strengthen programme ROI arguments in portfolio reviews.
A simple 'last major curriculum refresh' date per NYP programme, cross-referenced against the skills-trend feed, to flag which NYP offerings are due for review.
